items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The target CubeSat mission context, space and ground segments, intended users, and lifecycle flow from stakeholders to verification and validation are described.
evidence: intended to be used by system architects and engineers as a starting point as they develop the logical architecture of the Space and Ground components of the CubeSat mission of interest to them

The following subsections provide a notional outline of how the CSRM could be applied to a specific mission following a traditional top-down approach starting with identifying stakeholders and ending with verification and validation.

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?

evidence: The CSRM is a SysML compliant and platform-independent model that provides building blocks that can be specialized to support CubeSat mission design.

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The study is strong for describing a reusable SysML CubeSat reference-model structure, traceability, and notional application, but outcome evidence and reproducible implementation details are limited and EPS is only represented at generic system/subsystem level.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as core because the full text directly addresses CubeSat MBSE reference modeling, reuse, system-level traceability, and model-integrated V&V; EPS relevance is indirect through the generic Power Subsystem and historical power-usage trade studies.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Kaslow, D., Cahill, P. T., and Ayres, B. (2020). Development and Application of the CubeSat System Reference Model. DOI: 10.1109/aero47225.2020.9172714.
bibliographic_review_management.title: Development and Application of the CubeSat System Reference Model

RQ1.rationale: The paper substantially describes general CubeSat mission modeling with a reusable SysML reference model and generic subsystem abstractions, but does not provide a dedicated EPS behavior model.

RQ2.rationale: It claims system-level quality, reuse, common-baseline, and integrability benefits, but not EPS-specific reliability or measured EPS reproducibility outcomes.

RQ3.rationale: It describes model-integrated verification and validation activities linked to requirements and technical measures before physical realization, but not EPS-specific verification procedures.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper explicitly builds on prior CSRM/RAX, behavior, technical-measure, and integrated-simulation work in its references, but no other papers or prior extractions were read for this extraction.

RQ1: A CubeSat mission can be modeled generally through a SysML-compliant, platform-independent reference model covering stakeholders, requirements, behaviors, architecture, technical measures, and V&V.
The model handles limited mission-specific knowledge by providing generic, loosely defined subsystem packages and a library of elements that teams progressively populate and tailor.
EPS is not modeled in detail; the Power Subsystem appears only as a generic subsystem, with historical mention of power-usage behavior and solar/battery trade studies.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include quality enhancements, reuse economies, reduced development time, increased design quality, institutional knowledge transfer, common baseline comparison, and standards/reusable-library potential.
No explicit EPS reliability claim or measured reliability outcome is reported.

Evidence for reproducibility and integrability is mainly structural and qualitative: traceable model elements, conformance criteria, professional review, university use, and pending OMG specification activity.
RQ3: Verification and validation are integrated as model packages and activity elements with plans, procedures, execution notes, results, status, hyperlinks, and verifies/validates relationships.
